wrapscan.why: WS1, ruled 2026-07-23 (wrapscan S1 cold review, Mike's option A): the gate targets doctrine PROSE, and the record/log/review stores are deliberately one-line-per-entry for grep-ability and one-record-per-line diffs. Unscoped, docs/** measured ~6:1 noise to signal, which trains readers to ignore the gate. Cover given up: long prose lines outside the doctrine surface go unflagged.

spellscan.why: Ruled 2026-07-23 (Mike, on the queue-run-0959 spellscan apply): frozen historical record stores are kept VERBATIM — history is not retro-spelled, and the general-sense 'artifact' breaches living there are genuine NZ deviations left as-written on purpose. The gate protects NEW live prose. Cover given up: a US spelling entering a record store is not caught.

pathscan.why: PS4, landed 2026-07-28 (b012884): the gateable surface is the doctrine surface plus the live root files, with the record stores named OUT — a record describes the tree as it stood when written, and having no time axis it can never come clean without markers that would falsify it. Cover given up: a stale path reference inside a record is not flagged, which is the intended trade.
